### Reproducible Example

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import time

# Create two large DataFrames with missing data
np.random.seed(0)
size = 1_000_000

df1 = pd.DataFrame({
    'ID': range(size),
    'Name': np.random.choice(['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie', 'David', 'Eve', None], size)
})

df2 = pd.DataFrame({
    'ID': range(size // 2, size * 3 // 2),  # Overlapping and new IDs
    'Age': np.random.choice([None, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60], size)
})

# Measure time for merge operation
start_time = time.time()
merged_df = pd.merge(df1, df2, on='ID', how='outer')
merge_time = time.time() - start_time
print(f"Merge time: {merge_time:.2f} seconds")

# Measure time for fillna operation
start_time = time.time()
merged_df['Name'].fillna('Unknown', inplace=True)
merged_df['Age'].fillna(0, inplace=True)
fillna_time = time.time() - start_time
print(f"Fillna time: {fillna_time:.2f} seconds")

# Print some statistics
print(f"Total rows after merge: {len(merged_df)}")
print(f"Null values in 'Name' after fillna: {merged_df['Name'].isnull().sum()}")
print(f"Null values in 'Age' after fillna: {merged_df['Age'].isnull().sum()}")
```

title: ENH: Automate reading of data in chunks
body:
### Feature Type

- [x] Adding new functionality to pandas

- [ ] Changing existing functionality in pandas

- [ ] Removing existing functionality in pandas


### Problem Description

I have a file with 20Gb of data that I need to process. When I use a pandas dataframe, the full 20Gb need to be loaded. That will make the computer slow or even crash. Can this process be made more efficient by _automatically_ (very very important that the user does not have to do anything here) loads a chunk, processes it, writes it, loads the second chunk, etc. 

This is stuff is possible, it is done by [ROOT](https://root.cern/doc/master/classROOT_1_1RDataFrame.html) for instance.

### Feature Description

This would just work with the normal dataframes, there could be an option like

```python
pd.chunk_size = 100
```
which would process 100Mb at a time. So that no more than 100 Mb would be in memory.

### Alternative Solutions

Alternatively we can

```python
import ROOT

rdf = ROOT.RDataFrame('tree', 'path_to_file.root')
```

title: docs: add CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md for AI assistant codebase orientation
body:
## Background
AI coding assistants (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, etc.) benefit from a structured codebase orientation document placed at the repo root. This issue tracks the creation of `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` (same content, different naming conventions for different tools).

## Proposed Change
- Add `CLAUDE.md` — picked up by Claude Code automatically
- Add `AGENTS.md` — picked up by OpenAI Codex and similar agents

Both files cover:
- Top-level directory structure
- Component map (cmd/, pkg/, staging/)
- Build system (make targets, build scripts)
- Development workflows (code generation, verification, local dev)
- Test suite structure (unit, integration, e2e, node-e2e)
- API conventions and versioning
- Key conventions for contributors

title: HTTP/TCP probes with unresolved named port return Unknown and hide root cause ("port not found")
body:
### What happened?

For HTTP/TCP liveness/readiness/startup probes, port can be `intstr.IntOrString`.

In [ResolveContainerPort](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3c78e4355ac93436b4c95f39cf1ce576a3f8f41/pkg/probe/util.go#L27) does:
- try `findPortByName` for `intstr.String`
- if not found, fallback to `strconv.Atoi(param.StrVal)`

When probe uses a named port and name is wrong/missing (for example `controller`), kubelet emits:
```
Liveness probe errored and resulted in unknown state: strconv.Atoi: parsing "controller": invalid syntax
```
Then prober returns `probe.Unknown` in [runProbe](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3c78e4355ac93436b4c95f39cf1ce576a3f8f41/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober.go#L165).

Why this is problematic:
- Real reason (`port <name> not found`) is hidden by `strconv.Atoi` parse error.
- Behavior is inconsistent with numeric-port probes:
  - `int` port with unreachable endpoint -> regular probe failure path.
  - bad named port -> repeated `Unknown` events, not failure semantics.
- API validation for port names ([IsValidPortName](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c3c78e4355ac93436b4c95f39cf1ce576a3f8f41/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/validation/validation.go#L332)) requires at least one letter, so pure numeric strings are not valid named ports anyway; `Atoi` fallback in string branch is effectively misleading.

### What did you expect to happen?

If probe port is `intstr.String` and named port is not found:
- return explicit error like `port "<name>" not found` (no `Atoi` parse noise),
- and consider handling this case as probe `Failure` instead of `Unknown` to match practical liveness behavior.

Suggested direction:
1. Remove `Atoi` fallback from string branch in `ResolveContainerPort`.
2. Optionally add typed `ErrPortNotFound` and map it to `Failure` in prober.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-named-port-typo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Always
  containers:
  - name: pause
    image: registry.k8s.io/pause:latest
    ports:
    - name: metrics
      containerPort: 8080
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: metrcis # typo: should be "metrics"
      initialDelaySeconds: 1
      periodSeconds: 2
      timeoutSeconds: 1
      failureThreshold: 1
```

```bash
❯ k describe pod probe-named-port-typo
...
Warning  Unhealthy        48s (x25 over 96s)  kubelet            spec.containers{pause}: Liveness probe errored and resulted in unknown state: strconv.Atoi: parsing "metrcis": invalid syntax
```

title: ConfigMap BinaryData field not plumbed through to container env vars
body:
/sig node

During investigation of #139132, @liggitt noted:

> "none of the ConfigMap → Env transforms pull from the ConfigMap BinaryData field... that feels worth tracking in an issue to at least document"

Currently in `makeEnvironmentVariables()` in `pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go`, the `ConfigMapRef` (EnvFrom) path reads only from `configMap.Data` and ignores `configMap.BinaryData`. Similarly, `ConfigMapKeyRef` (Env) only reads from `configMap.Data`.

This means binary data stored in `ConfigMap.BinaryData` cannot be used as a container env var source, even though the API allows it.

This should be documented at minimum, and ideally either:
- Plumbed through (with appropriate encoding considerations), or  
- Explicitly rejected with a clear error message

Related: #139132, #139168
label: actionable

title: Convert the DisruptionMode from enum to struct
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Convert the DisruptionMode field in the API from a primitive string enum pointer `DisruptionMode string` to a struct pointer `DisruptionMode struct` to support future extensibility.

```
type DisruptionMode struct {
    Type DisruptionModeType `json:"type,omitempty"`
}
```

Since the change is backward incompatible, the new `v1alpha3` API version will be introduced and `v1alpha2` abandoned. Intoducing new API version is tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/138575

### Why is this needed?

Support `DisruptionMode` extensibility since a single value enum may not be sufficient.
label: actionable

title: Properly handle minCount during workload preemption
body:
Right now our workload preemption removes as many victims as possible as long as the workload fits. The workload fits as long as minCount pods or more are scheduled. This makes us:
1. Reprieve as many victims as possible
2. Prefer scheduling minCount pods if it allows us to reprieve more pod groups/pods.  

When we're preempting for a pod group, we want to
1. Schedule as many of its pods as possible
2. Reprieve as many victims as long as above condition is satisfied

/sig scheduling
/assign

title: ImageLocality counts ImageVolume images in raw score but not in max threshold
body:
### What happened?

PR #130231 updated the `ImageLocality` plugin to account for ImageVolume images when scoring nodes.

However, the current implementation appears to include ImageVolume images only in the raw image score calculation, but not in the image count used to derive the max score threshold.

In `Score`, `imageScores` is calculated by `sumImageScores`:

```go
imageScores := sumImageScores(nodeInfo, pod, totalNumNodes)

score := calculatePriority(imageScores, len(pod.Spec.InitContainers)+len(pod.Spec.Containers))
```

After #130231, sumImageScores includes image volumes:

```go
for _, volume := range pod.Spec.Volumes {
	if volume.Image == nil {
		continue
	}

	if state, ok := nodeInfo.GetImageStates()[normalizedImageName(volume.Image.Reference)]; ok {
		sum += scaledImageScore(state, totalNumNodes)
	}
}
```

But the second argument passed to calculatePriority still counts only init containers and regular containers:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```
calculatePriority then uses this count to derive the max threshold:

```go
maxThreshold := maxContainerThreshold * int64(numContainers)
```

This means ImageVolume images increase the raw image score, but do not increase the max threshold. As a result, Pods using ImageVolume can receive a higher ImageLocality score, or reach MaxNodeScore more easily, because ImageVolume images are counted in the numerator but not in the threshold.

### What did you expect to happen?

I think this is a bug because, from the perspective of ImageLocality scoring, a container image and an ImageVolume image have the same locality effect: both are images required by the Pod, and both can avoid image pulling cost if they already exist on the node.

Therefore, ImageVolume images should be counted consistently in ImageLocality scoring.

Since #130231 made ImageVolume images contribute to sumImageScores, they should also contribute to the image count passed to calculatePriority.

The image count should be based on:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers) + numberOfImageVolumes
```

rather than only:

```go
len(pod.Spec.InitContainers) + len(pod.Spec.Containers)
```

With this behavior, a Pod with one regular container image plus one ImageVolume image would be scored consistently with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use a Pod with one regular container image and one ImageVolume image.

For example:

```go
testImageVolume := v1.PodSpec{
	Containers: []v1.Container{
		{
			Image: "gcr.io/30",
		},
	},
	Volumes: []v1.Volume{
		{
			Name: "imageVolume",
			VolumeSource: v1.VolumeSource{
				Image: &v1.ImageVolumeSource{
					Reference: "gcr.io/300",
				},
			},
		},
	},
}
```

Assume there are two nodes:

```go
nodes := []*v1.Node{
	makeImageNode("node1", node300600900),
	makeImageNode("node2", node400030),
}
```

For node1, the ImageVolume image gcr.io/300:latest is already present.

Current behavior calculates the score as if there were only one image source:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M - 23M) = 12
```

If ImageVolume images are included in the image count, the score should be calculated with two image sources:

```
100 * (300M * 1/2 - 23M) / (1000M * 2 - 23M) = 6
```

This would make the ImageVolume case consistent with a Pod that has the same two images as regular container images.

title: client-go certificate manager hardcodes ECDSA P-256 key type with no way to configure it
body:
### What happened?

The `generateCSR()` function in `staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go` hardcodes the key type to ECDSA P-256:

```go
privateKey, err := ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), cryptorand.Reader)
```

This means all kubelet client and server certificates generated via the certificate manager use ECDSA P-256, regardless of what key type the cluster CA uses. There is no configuration option to override this.

The kubelet client certificate on the first control plane node is initially generated by `kubeadm` using the same key type as the cluster CA (typically RSA 2048), but on subsequent rotations it switches to ECDSA P-256 because rotation goes through client-go's hardcoded path.

### What did you expect to happen?

The key type for CSR generation should be configurable via the `CertificateManager` `Config` struct, similar to how `GetUsages` is already a configurable function. For example:

```go
type Config struct {
    // ...existing fields...

    // GenerateKey allows overriding the default key generation (ECDSA P-256).
    // If nil, defaults to ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), rand.Reader).
    GenerateKey func() (crypto.Signer, error)
}
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy a Kubernetes cluster with an RSA CA (default `kubeadm init` behavior).
2. Inspect the kubelet client certificate on the first control plane node — it uses RSA (same as CA).
3. Wait for certificate rotation (or force it by shortening cert lifetime).
4. After rotation, inspect the new kubelet client certificate — it is now ECDSA P-256.
5. On worker nodes, kubelet client and server certificates are ECDSA P-256 from the start.

The hardcoded line is at:
[`staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go#L767`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/certificate/certificate_manager.go#L767)

### Anything else we need to know?

- Environments requiring RSA keys (compliance, HSM compatibility, consistency with CA) cannot use built-in certificate rotation without patching client-go.
- Some deployments require ECDSA P-384 as P-256 is not considered sufficient under their security policies. The hardcoded P-256 makes this impossible without forking client-go.
- The `GetUsages` callback already handles the key-type-dependent usage selection, so the infrastructure for key-type awareness exists — only the generation itself is not configurable.

title: apiserver: return 4xx instead of 500 for invalid kind type in version/kind decoding
body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes API Server returns HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when handling a DELETE request whose request body contains an invalid `kind` field type.

In the following request, the `kind` field is set to a boolean value instead of a string. This is an invalid client request, but the API Server returns HTTP 500:

```bash
curl -X DELETE 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/apis/apiregistration.k8s.io/v1/apiservices' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"kind":true}'
```
Actual response:
```bash
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "couldn't get version/kind; json parse error: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field .kind of type string",
  "code": 500
}
```
A similar behavior can also be triggered on validatingwebhookconfigurations:
```bash
curl -X DELETE 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/apis/admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1/validatingwebhookconfigurations' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"kind":true}'
```
The response also returns HTTP 500 with the same kind of version/kind decoding error.

### What did you expect to happen?

```markdown
The API Server should treat this as an invalid client request and return a 4xx response, such as HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity, instead of HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.

The response should report that the `kind` field has an invalid type, rather than exposing it as an internal server error.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Start a Kubernetes cluster with Kubernetes v1.33.1.
2. Start the local API proxy:

```bash
kubectl proxy --port=8001
```
3. Send the following request:
```bash
curl -X DELETE 'http://127.0.0.1:8001/apis/apiregistration.k8s.io/v1/apiservices' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"kind":true}'
````
4.Observe that the API Server returns HTTP 500:
```bash
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "couldn't get version/kind; json parse error: json: cannot unmarshal bool into Go struct field .kind of type string",
  "code": 500
}
```

### Anything else we need to know?

```markdown
This issue was found during RESTful API fuzzing of the Kubernetes API Server.

The request body is clearly malformed because `kind` should be a string. Therefore, the behavior appears to be an error classification problem: the invalid request is surfaced as an internal server error instead of a client-side validation or decoding error.

In my test, this behavior is reproducible on Kubernetes v1.33.1.

title: AddPod uses return instead of continue when probe worker already exists
body:
/sig node
/kind cleanup

The AddPod function in `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go` uses return instead of continue when it finds a probe worker that already exists. This exits the entire function, silently skipping all remaining containers in the loop. The correct statement is continue, which skips only the current probe and continues processing the rest.

The log message itself says "**already exists for container**"  meaning skip this container, not abort the whole function. The behavior contradicts the stated intent.
same for all three probes 

```
 if _, ok := m.workers[key]; ok {
				logger.V(8).Info("Startup probe already exists for container",
                       	"pod", klog.KObj(pod), "containerName", c.Name)
                             return
}
```

Affected lines:  `pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go` lines 199, 211, 223 (startup, readiness, liveness checks respectively)

So fix would be continue instead of return in all three lines.

title: ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-golang-tip and ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip failing: undefined: http2.TrailerPrefix under Go tip go1.27
body:
### Which jobs are failing?

- [`ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-golang-tip`](https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-golang-tip)
- [`ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip`](https://prow.k8s.io/job-history/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip)

### Which tests are failing?

Build fails before tests run:
`vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/internal/transport/handler_server.go:271:18: undefined: http2.TrailerPrefix`

### Since when has it been failing?

Both jobs went red on 2026-05-22 ~22:00 UTC.

- e2e-kind: last green [2057881334864416768](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-golang-tip/2057881334864416768) (Go tip `fc245b6427`), first red [2057941985288785920](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-kind-golang-tip/2057941985288785920) (Go tip `99675026a7`).
- unit: last green [2057884102870175744](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip/2057884102870175744), first red [2057944767483875328](https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-unit-golang-tip/2057944767483875328).

K8s SHA was effectively unchanged across the boundary; only the Go tip toolchain moved. Rev `99675026a7` is the first identifying as `go1.27`.

### Root cause

Vendored `golang.org/x/net v0.54.0` defines `TrailerPrefix` only in `http2/server.go`, which carries `//go:build !(go1.27 && !http2legacy)` and is therefore excluded under `go1.27`. Neither `server_wrap.go` nor `server_common.go` defines it.

Fixed upstream by golang/net commit [1efab4271a](https://github.com/golang/net/commit/1efab4271a7ba50c37ae8d1d8dd67585a452518d) ("http2: avoid API changes when built with go1.27", ref golang/go#78508), which moves `TrailerPrefix` (and other dropped symbols) into `server_common.go`. Included in `golang.org/x/net v0.55.0` (tagged 2026-05-22).

### Proposed fix

Bump `golang.org/x/net` from v0.54.0 to v0.55.0.

title: [sig-network] Conntrack proxy implementation should not be vulnerable to the invalid conntrack state bug [Privileged] failing due to bug in test, again
body:
This is a reincarnation of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134116.

I have recently started to notice `[sig-network] Conntrack proxy implementation should not be vulnerable to the invalid conntrack state bug [Privileged]` flakes in downstream OpenShift CI jobs, statistically more significant in dual-stack (but not only).

We got a fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134164 for this which introduced tracking via

```
ipPort := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", addr.String(), pkt.DestPort)
[...]
pending[ipPort] = pkt.Seq + 1
```

instead of only

```
pending[addr.String()] = pkt.Seq + 1
```

however from my brief analysis it seems that we should be actually tracking by

```
ipPort := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", addr.String(), pkt.SrcPort)
```

so that we create a key using client's ephemeral port, not the server's listening port.

title: Provide some mechanism for HTTP errors to fall back to global ErrorHandler when withFetch / FetchBackend is enabled
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are relevant/related to the feature request?

common

### Description

My team just attempted to enable `withFetch()` in our application and encountered a pretty major footgun - because the FetchBackend runs outside the Angular zone, any HTTP errors, JSON parsing errors, etc. that occur and aren't caught downstream in a subscription go completely uncaught. If the HTTP request occurred during server side rendering, this results in the app _crashing_ altogether.

This was unexpected and we only diagnosed why our app was crashing in certain environments after doing some very deep server-side debugging into the source of the error. This difference isn't documented anywhere that I can find.

### Proposed solution

It would be helpful if there was some mechanism to ensure that errors that occur during HTTP requests when the HttpClient is configured with `withFetch` are still able to fall back to the global error handler. I'm not sure what that would look like -- maybe configuration that can be passed into the `withFetch()` call?

### Alternatives considered

Everywhere we make an HTTP request _should_ already have explicit error handling, but there are a lot of places that don't have it in our codebase. These are mostly not on purpose (just oversights when implementing new features years ago), and those places have never caused any major issues because the global error handler catches the errors when HttpClient uses the XHR backend.

We already have logging set up in our global error handler to inform us when server-side network requests are failing like this so we can address them and add proper error handling, and for the sake of reliability we would prefer to catch failing network requests this way (rather than the entire application going down in production.) Our global error handler also adds some metadata to these errors that can be helpful when debugging; the app crashing altogether is a lot harder to debug because the error is more confusing and does not include that metadata.

Thank you!
label: needs_info

However, the application only runs if I add DatePipe to the providers array in main.ts within my test harness. This shouldn’t be a requirement for a component library—I want to avoid tightly coupling the library to any consuming application in this way. ### Minimal Reproduction Here are the steps to reproduce the issue: ### **Steps to Reproduce the "No Provider for DatePipe" Error in Angular 19 Component Library** #### **1. Create a New Angular Component Library** - Generate a new Angular workspace with a library: ```sh ng new my-workspace --create-application=false cd my-workspace ng generate library my-lib ``` - Navigate to the `projects/my-lib` directory. #### **2. Create a Component That Uses `DatePipe`** - Inside `projects/my-lib/src/lib/`, create a new component: ```sh ng generate component date-display ``` - Modify `date-display.component.ts` to use `DatePipe`: ```typescript import { Component, Inject } from '@angular/core'; import { DatePipe } from '@angular/common'; @Component({ selector: 'lib-date-display', template: '

{{ today | date }}

', providers: [DatePipe] // Providing DatePipe here }) export class DateDisplayComponent { today = new Date(); constructor(private datePipe: DatePipe) { console.log(this.datePipe.transform(this.today, 'longDate')); } } ``` #### **3. Ensure `NgModule` is Removed (Standalone Component)** - Modify `date-display.component.ts` to make it a standalone component: ```typescript @Component({ selector: 'lib-date-display', standalone: true, template: '

{{ today | date }}

', providers: [DatePipe] // Providing DatePipe here }) export class DateDisplayComponent { today = new Date(); constructor(private datePipe: DatePipe) { console.log(this.datePipe.transform(this.today, 'longDate')); } } ``` #### **4. Build the Library** - Run: ```sh ng build my-lib ``` - The build should succeed without errors. #### **5. Create a Test Application** - Generate a new Angular application to test the library: ```sh ng generate application test-app ``` - Add the library to the application: ```sh ng add my-lib ``` #### **6. Use the Component in the Test Application** - Open `test-app/src/app/app.component.html` and add: ```html ``` - Open `test-app/src/app/app.component.ts` and import the standalone component: ```typescript import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { DateDisplayComponent } from 'my-lib'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', standalone: true, imports: [DateDisplayComponent], template: '' }) export class AppComponent {} ``` #### **7. Run the Application** ```sh ng serve test-app ``` - **Expected Behavior:** The app should run without issues. - **Actual Behavior:** A runtime error occurs: ``` Error: NG0203: No provider for DatePipe! ``` #### **8. Workaround: Add `DatePipe` to `main.ts`** - Modify `test-app/src/main.ts` to provide `DatePipe` globally: ```typescript import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser'; import { AppComponent } from './app/app.component'; import { provideHttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'; import { DatePipe } from '@angular/common'; bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, { providers: [DatePipe] }); ``` - **Now the application runs correctly.** ### **Issue Summary** - The component library builds successfully. - Despite providing `DatePipe` at the component level, Angular still throws a "No Provider" error at runtime. - The app only works when `DatePipe` is provided at the application level (`main.ts`), which **forces tight coupling** between the library and the consuming application. ### **Expected Behavior** - Since `DatePipe` is provided in the standalone component, the app should not require an additional provider in `main.ts`. - The component library should be self-contained and not require the consuming application to explicitly provide `DatePipe`. title: ng extract-i18n crashes with startOfLinePositions error when consuming a packaged library in Angular 20 Nx workspace (regression from Angular 19)
body:
### Command

extract-i18n

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

19.2.9

### Description

Hi, 

I'm actually facing an issue after migrating from Angular 19 to Angular 20. Below relatives informations about the issue:

**Summary**

When running ng extract-i18n in an Angular 20 Nx workspace that consumes a published Angular library, the extraction fails with:

`./node_modules/@myCompany/mylib/fesm2022/mylib.mjs - Error: Module build failed (from ./node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/src/builders/extract-i18n/ivy-extract-loader.js):
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startOfLinePositions')
`

**Regression**

This problem did not occur in Angular 19.
The error only started appearing after upgrading the Nx workspace and the library to Angular 20 (with TypeScript 5.9.2).
The same library and setup worked fine under Angular 19.

**Details**

Workspace setup:
- Nx monorepo with Angular 20.2.3
- Libraries built with @nx/angular:package (ng-packagr under the hood)
- TypeScript 5.9.2
- The consuming app installs the packaged library from node_modules (no paths alias).
- The published library includes source maps:

The published library includes source maps:
- index.d.ts.map files with "sources" pointing to local monorepo paths such as:
`"../../../libs/my-lib/src/lib/interfaces/my-component-interface.interface.ts"
`
- .mjs.map files with "sources" pointing to temporary build paths such as:

`../tmp-esm2022/lib/components/...`

These paths don’t exist in the consumer app. When ng extract-i18n traverses them, it fails deep inside the TypeScript compiler (startOfLinePositions).

**Observations**

The error occurs only when consuming the library as a packaged dependency from node_modules.
If the app consumes the sources directly via paths, extract-i18n works.

Both app and lib use Angular 20.2.3 + TypeScript 5.9.2 + tslib 2.8.1.

**Expected Behavior**

ng extract-i18n should not crash if a dependency includes sourcemaps pointing to unavailable sources.

It should:

- Ignore those sourcemaps, or fail gracefully with a clear error, or provide a configuration option to disable sourcemap consumption during i18n extraction.


### Minimal Reproduction

1) Create an Nx workspace with Angular 20
2) Generate a publishable Angular library
3) Enable sourcemaps in the library (the failing case)

```
{
  "extends": "../tsconfig.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": true,
    "sourceMap": true,
    "inlineSources": false
  },
  "angularCompilerOptions": {
    "compilationMode": "partial"
  }
}
```

4) Build the library
This creates dist/libs/digital-components-kit/ containing:
- fesm2022/…mjs and …mjs.map (with ../tmp-esm2022/... in "sources")
- index.d.ts and index.d.ts.map (with ../../../libs/.../*.ts in "sources")

5) Create an Angular app in the same workspace
Install the library into the app from dist (local file install to simulate a packaged dependency)
Important: Do not use a TS paths alias to the sources. The app should import from node_modules/@demo/digital-components-kit.

6) Run i18n extraction (failing)

Observed error (example):
./node_modules/@myCompany/mylib/fesm2022/mylib.mjs - Error: Module build failed (from ./node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/src/builders/extract-i18n/ivy-extract-loader.js):

body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

platform-browser

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

When running unit tests for a component that uses `ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom` an error is thrown `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'elements' of 'this.registry' as it is undefined.`. This was introduced in v20.2.0 and works in v20.1.8. In my case this seems to happen when calling `fixture.detectChanges()`

Upon investigation it looks like changes in `dom_renderer.js` are causing the issue. `this.registry` is defined as the return value of the function `getAnimationElementRemovalRegistry` - [see here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/9e172e0280549caf59d5b2025b2f09b7bae3477a/packages/platform-browser/src/dom/dom_renderer.ts#L167). This then causes an issue in the `removeChild` function, the following line doesn't work as `this.registry` isn't defined

```
const { elements } = this.registry;
```

[see file here](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/9e172e0280549caf59d5b2025b2f09b7bae3477a/packages/platform-browser/src/dom/dom_renderer.ts#L339).

Seems to only be throwing the error specifically with `ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom` set.

It occurs in version 20.2.0 and above

body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

common

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

In Angular 18.1.1, using HttpClient.options(..., { observe: 'response' }), the Allow header from the response is not available when the response has status 204 No Content, even though:

- The server includes Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Allow
- The Allow header is present and visible in the browser Network tab
- Plain fetch() can read the Allow header without issue

However, when the backend changes the response to **200 OK** (instead of **204 No Content**), Angular’s HttpClient correctly exposes the Allow header.

Tested with a standard OGC API Features service — spec requires use of Allow header.

**Expected behavior:**
HttpClient should expose all headers listed in Access-Control-Expose-Headers, regardless of status code — including when status is 204.

**Actual behavior:**
When status is 204 No Content, HttpClient does not expose the Allow header (but fetch() does).

title: @angular/core/primitives/di export collision with @angular/core breaks SystemJS bundling
body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

Yes

### Description

#### Problem
When bundling Angular 20+ for SystemJS (required for micro-frontends), the `inject` export from `@angular/core/primitives/di` collides with the public `inject` `export from @angular/core`. This causes bundlers to silently drop one of the exports, breaking runtime behavior.

#### Context

Use case: Micro-frontends using SystemJS for module loading
Angular version: 20+ (affects all versions with `primitives/di`)
Bundler: Rollup (same issue likely affects Webpack with SystemJS output)

Starting in Angular 20, the `fesm2022/` output includes chunked ESM with shared internal modules extracted into separate files. When creating a merged SystemJS bundle that includes both `@angular/core` and its sub-paths, Rollup encounters:
```javascript
export * from '@angular/core';
export * from '@angular/core/primitives/di';
```
Both modules export a function named `inject`, causing an ambiguous export conflict. Rollup silently drops one of them during the merge, resulting in missing exports in the final SystemJS output.

While I've found a workaround, other teams using micro-frontends and shared SystemJS bundles are struggling to resolve this. The issue creates real blockers for legitimate architectural patterns in the Angular ecosystem.

Attempts to resolve: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/67098

The red underline remains only on ``. --- ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Ionic Angular project (standalone) 2. Place any image in `src/assets` 3. Add this to any template: 4. VSCode shows a red underline on the `` tag or `src` attribute 5. Run the app: ionic serve 6. The image displays correctly and no runtime or build errors occur --- ## Expected behavior A valid `` tag with a correct `src` path should not be flagged as an error. --- ## Actual behavior VSCode shows a red underline (error) on `` even though: - The code is valid - The image exists - The app runs correctly - No Angular compiler errors occur This appears to be a false-positive from Angular Language Service. --- ## Environment - Angular: 17.x - Ionic: 7.x - VSCode: latest - Angular Language Service: latest - OS: Windows 11 - Project type: Standalone --- ## Additional notes - This issue does not occur in Angular 16 or earlier. - This issue does not occur with other HTML tags. - The error cannot be suppressed by any known configuration. - This affects development experience because only `` is always marked as an error. --- Note: I do not speak English, so I prepared this report with the help of Microsoft Copilot.
